$comment: D-CSUBSET-LINKAGE-INHERITED-INTERNAL-EMITS-GLOBAL (C 6.2.2p4/p5): a plain definition whose linkage is INHERITED from a visible prior `static` declaration is INTERNAL, so two TUs may each carry their own. THE EXAMPLE MUST BE TWO TUs — the single-TU form already compiled and ran correctly before the fix, and a single-TU image carries no symbol table that could contradict the binding, so a one-file pin could not fail. left.c and right.c each use the inheritance shape for a FUNCTION (`static int tuValue(void); int tuValue(void){…}`) and for an INITIALIZED OBJECT (`static int tuSlot; int tuSlot = 1;` — the ordering where the definition OUTRANKS the static tentative in the redeclaration merge and becomes the emitting declaration). leftTotal()=20+1=21, rightTotal()=30+4=34, exit 55; a silent re-merge onto left.c's copies would give 42, and the pre-fix compiler refused the program outright with K_SymbolRedefinedAcrossUnits. REFERENCES probed SEPARATELY 2026-09-01 on this two-file shape: gcc 13.3.0, clang 18.1.3 and MSVC 19.51 all BUILD AND RUN the function half; the object half splits (gcc + clang reject `static int g; int g = 4;`, MSVC accepts it and classes the symbol `Static` in its own .obj — one accepting reference makes it REQUIRED and states the meaning). RED-ON-DISABLE: in `recordLinkage` (src/hir/lowering/cst_to_hir.cpp) drop the `rec->isInternalLinkage` arm so the binding folds from the definition's own specifier tokens again -> K_SymbolRedefinedAcrossUnits on 'tuValue'. Legs mirror bare_proto_crosscu / block_scope_extern.
